entities.summary: Giovanni Battista del Tasso (1500–1555) was a renowned Italian architect and sculptor whose contributions to Renaissance art and architecture had a lasting impact on the development of urban planning and civic design in Italy. Born in Mantua, Italy, del Tasso's work was characterized by its innovative use of perspective and its emphasis on creating harmonious and balanced spaces. His most famous work, the Palazzo Farnese in Rome, is still celebrated for its beauty and historical significance today. Del Tasso's influence can be seen in the works of later architects, such as Andrea Palladio, and his legacy continues to inspire architects and artists around the world.
